Register the repo-wide md-lint CI job (from shipment 106-S / feature 126-F) as a REQUIRED status check via GitHub branch protection. The gate is repo-wide and blocking from its first run (0 violations repo-wide via the MD025 _title config + the ~21 structural remediations), so NO advisory cycle is needed — this supersedes the earlier advisory-first framing. Branch-protection required-status-check configuration is done in the GitHub repo settings OUTSIDE the repository tree (not a code/CI file change), so it needs an operator/admin action and cannot be a normal in-repo Ship task. Refs: 126-F, 126.004-T, docs/exec-plans/2026-07-25-markdownlint-p008-provisioning-plan.md, deliberation 054-DL.

durable_writes second-layer hardening: complete ErrWriteIndeterminate caller reconciliation and retry-idempotency before durable mode is promoted toward default/GA. Surfaced by Copilot review cycle-4 on PR #308 (feature 123-F, shipment 109-S). All items are opt-in (durable_writes default=false) and triple-gated (durable ON + fsync failure + retry); MD is source of truth and the SQLite index self-heals on sync, so severity is P2. Acceptance criteria: (1) UnarchiveItem non-git branch (archive.go ~770): on ErrWriteIndeterminate from the restore write, complete-or-rollback the restore instead of returning early and leaving archive copy + DB row + duplicate files with no recovery. (2) persistArtifact Site-1 (shipment.go ~390): legacy callers AddDependency/RemoveDependency treat every error as file-untouched and roll back the DB edge; add explicit ErrWriteIndeterminate handling/reconciliation so durable-mode fsync failure does not diverge MD from the live index (or document reliance on sync-rebuild). (3) appendDurable (events/stream.go ~171): after a parent-dir fsync fails, a retry early-returns and never re-fsyncs the parent, so a later append can report success while the logs dir is not power-loss durable — make the durable append retry re-attempt the parent flush (ErrWriteNotApplied safe-retry contract). (4) mkdirAllDurable (durable_fs.go ~39): if mkdir succeeds but the parent fsync fails, the os.Stat early-return on retry skips the failed flush permanently — make durable mkdir retry re-fsync the parent of an already-existing dir when its dirent durability was not confirmed. (5) MCP writer durable mode (mcp/server.go ~76): append_comment can surface ErrWriteIndeterminate but the handler maps every append failure to a generic internal error; map both durability classes (not-applied vs indeterminate) to explicit machine-readable MCP outcomes so agents do not duplicate comments on retry.
